newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-WENGER'S OFFICE DESTROYED BY FIRE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-WENGER'S OFFICE DESTROYED BY FIRE.

text.p: The office of new Arsenal manager Arsene Wenger was destroyed by a fire at the club's training ground north of London, fire brigade officials said on Tuesday.

The fire, believed to have started in a washing machine during a raging storm on Monday night, caused thousands of pounds worth of damage at the training ground at London Colney, 20 miles from Arsenal's Highbury stadium.
The extent of damage was still being assessed by local firemen on Tuesday.
Ten fire-fighting appliances attended the blaze which took three hours to bring under control in Force 8 gales which made the work doubly hazardous and difficult.

The grounds and a separate building which houses a canteen and recreation area escaped damage but a fire brigade spokesman said there was evidence the blaze was caused by an electrical fault on a tumble-dry washing-machine.
"Luckily nobody was around at the time and nobody was hurt but it was an extremely perilous operation for our people," said the spokesman.
Arsenal's players trained at Highbury on Tuesday and may have to look for a temporary site with suitable facilities.
